text:
Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Lowen Ridge, the company announced on 14 March 2025.

Marisol Entwhistle, the company's Chief Operations Officer, confirmed the site selection at a press briefing in Lowen Ridge, which this reporter attended. Speaking to the assembled journalists, she said the choice follows months of review.

The depot is budgeted at 212 million credits and is expected to employ 640 workers once it is running.

The decision rests on Kestrelline Rail's "Regional Fleet Readiness Plan 2025–2032," the document presented at the briefing. Copies were handed out at the door, and the depot's location was set out in its pages.

Ms. Entwhistle took questions after her remarks. The Gazette will continue to follow the project as it moves forward.
